configs.description: The cable manager as Hubbell ships HM14C, the cover fitted.
configs.name: base

configs.description: The same manager with the cover taken off, the five rings in front of the plate in view.
configs.name: cover-off

gaps.note: the sheet's figure marks a dimension D for the rings behind the plate and its table gives A, B and C only. Taken as equal to C, read off the figure against it.
gaps.wanted: the dimensioned customer drawing, or the maker's figure for D

gaps.note: the sheet's figure shows each wire ring bent round where it leaves the plate and at its free end, with a hook on the post of alternate rings, and dimensions none of it. The side views draw the loop with a 11.43 mm corner radius (two wire diameters), a stand-in; the 3D loop keeps square corners and no hook is drawn. The rings are drawn in a mid steel tone so they read against the black plate; the sheet states none.
gaps.wanted: the dimensioned customer drawing, or the maker's figure for the ring's bend and hook

gaps.note: the sheet's figure shows a folded edge along the cover, the HM24C photograph a lip along the top and a name plate at the middle. The face draws a 6 mm fold along the top and foot and the plate's 58 by 12 mm box blank; the fold's width is a stand-in.

the sheet calls the cover "hinged & removable" and its figure draws it swung open; the format has no hinge, so the cover is one panel drawn fitted, and the `cover-off` configuration is the cover taken off.
gaps.wanted: a format for a hinge; nothing the maker could add

gaps.note: the sheet states no count of cables, nor a basis for one; it says only that the rings align with the patch panel's adaptors.
gaps.wanted: a maker's figure with its basis
`attrs.physical.weight-kg` (profile `passive` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - material, wire diameter and finish are the sheet's specification table; the cover, the pass-through holes and the corresponding vertical manager are its characteristics table; the UPC is its ordering table.

cable-capacity.note: datasheet - the sheet states no cable capacity, so none is stated here and none is estimated.

chassis.note: datasheet - 482.6 x 44.45 x 204.7. Width is B, 19 in; height is A, 1.75 in, which the figure marks along the plate's end, so it is the plate; ru is the sheet's 1 RU. Depth is the overall: the sheet's C, 4 in (101.6 mm) in front of the plate, the plate's thickness, and the rear extension D behind it. The sheet's own "Depth 4 in" is C alone.

ears.note: estimated - `positions` states where the part bolts, for the Rack Builder. The plate is the part's own ears, so the rail plane is the back of the plate: the front rings stand C, 101.6, out of its front, and the plate is 1.5 thick (estimated), so `at` is 103.1. The five rings behind it reach into the rack by D (see `rear-extension`). The sheet's accessories list a replacement cover and hook-and-loop ties and no rail kit, so `kits` is not stated.

front.note: estimated - the front: the plate with its four windows, five wire rings and the cover. The figure has no scale, so the ring pitch and the window sizes are read against B (see the plate's `windows`): five rings 112 mm apart, symmetric about the middle, a ring in the web between each pair of windows and one at each end, as the figure draws them. The cover is drawn fitted; the `cover-off` configuration leaves it off and shows the rings.

full-depth.note: `full-depth: false` - the rings reach 101.6 in front of the rail and 101.6 behind it, not the depth of the rack, so the rack unit's rear face is not claimed.

left.note: estimated - an elevation, rear on the left: each ring's wires and post, either side of the plate's edge. The right is the same, turned round.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S OWN SPEC SHEET. Hubbell publishes one PDF per catalogue number, PREMISE_HM14C_spec.pdf on hubbellcdn.com (sha256 below): a features list, an ordering table, specifications, characteristics, accessories and a dimensions table, A 1 RU, 1.75 in (44), B 19 in (483), C 4 in (102), beside one isometric figure that marks A, B, C and D. The sheet's "Customer Use Drawing" link points at ecatalog.hubbell-premise.com, which does not resolve (checked 2026-10-18). Hubbell's CDN does serve a CAD drawing of this family, a .dwg in AutoCAD 2018 format (hubbellcdn.com/customerusedrawing/HWS14421C-HM1xx_1U_HOR_CBL_ORG.dwg, 382,784 bytes, linked from the HM144C sheet); nothing on the build host opens a DWG, so it was not read. No dimensioned drawing was read: the sheet's figure is a line drawing without a scale, and everything read off it is `estimated`, with how.

rear.note: estimated - the figure draws a second set of five rings on the far side of the plate, its dimension D; they are the front's, seen from behind, with the same windows.

rear-extension.note: estimated - 101.6, as C. The figure marks a fourth dimension D for the rings behind the plate, and no table gives it. Read on the HM14C, HM24C and HM34C figures against C the same way, D is 0.98, 0.90 and 1.10 of it, so the two are taken as equal; Hubbell's own page for the HM144C, the 1-unit part that states a 4 in rear extension, agrees. No sheet says the HM14C has the same rear extension as the HM144C.

thickness.note: estimated - 1.5 mm. No Hubbell sheet states the plate's gauge for the M-Series.

top.note: estimated - an elevation: the plate's edge and the ten rings' top wires, five behind it and five in front. The cover's edge is not drawn: the configuration with it off draws the same plan.
